claims: `ui-dashboard/src/lib/canonical-revenue/actuals.ts:30-45` — dormant wallets still kill the series through the staleness path: `latestReserveSnapshotBucketsBySource` counts every source key as an active reserve source, including the all-zero stETH wallets this commit just taught `daily-series.ts` to ignore

If a dormant wallet's rows lag the active wallet's by even one day, `reserveStaleAfterBucket` (`actuals.ts:47-65`) pins `reserveStaleAfter` to the dormant wallet's last bucket and nulls all reserve revenue after it

`ui-dashboard/src/lib/canonical-revenue/daily-series.ts:76-83` — guard is narrower than its own rationale: `isZeroExposureStethSnapshot` requires all four fields zero, but only `totalEarnedYieldAmount` and `dailyEarnedYieldAmount` are ever multiplied by `usdPerToken`. A wallet holding 100 stETH with zero accrued yield so far contributes exactly `0` to the history regardless of price, yet still trips `reserveHistoryUnpriced` and nulls the entire reserve series — including unrelated sUSDS revenue

`ui-dashboard/src/lib/canonical-revenue/daily-series.ts:69-73` — dead `try`/`catch`: after `/^-?\d+$/` passes on the trimmed string, `BigInt(trimmed)` cannot throw. The `catch { return false }` is unreachable

`ui-dashboard/src/lib/__tests__/canonical-revenue.test.ts:354-408` — the 11 negative cases never exercise the priced path: both `it.each` blocks use `reserveYield()` with the default `holdings: []`, so `stethRates` is empty and every assertion holds because `usdPerToken === undefined` short-circuits at `daily-series.ts:136`
The four `"not-wei"` cases are redundant with the `catch` and none of the 11 cover a *priced* wallet with a malformed field

A priced wallet with a malformed field currently reports the misleading `"…USD/token pricing is missing."` when the real problem is unparseable data (pre-existing message bug, but the new tests give the impression it's covered)

Pre-existing: a priced wallet whose cumulative `totalEarnedYieldAmount` drops (e.g. `unrealizedYieldAmount` falling when balance dips below principal) books a large negative day and a matching positive rebound, spiking the daily chart

judge_reasoning.3830423746: The review affirmatively denies this: it states the zero-return cannot corrupt cumulative-delta arithmetic and that for priced wallets the guard is a no-op. Its 'aside' about a negative day comes from a cumulative total dropping and is explicitly called identical on base and branch / pre-existing, not the fabricated negative spike created by returning 0 on a full-withdrawal day via the baselineUsd fallback.
judge_reasoning.3830513980: No mention of transfers between tracked wallets, recordTransfer, principal/balance movement, or the need to subtract prior unrealized yield when a wallet is emptied; findings all concern staleness, guard breadth, dead try/catch, and test coverage.

1.why: actuals.ts:25-45 keys every row (incl. all-zero stETH wallets) as a separate source and reserveStaleAfterBucket (47-65) takes the min over all of them, so the new zero-exposure notion in daily-series.ts is not applied to the staleness path at all.

3.why: Only totalEarnedYieldAmount (line 121) and dailyEarnedYieldAmount (line 153) are priced; balanceAmount/principalAmount are used nowhere but the guard, so a nonzero-balance/zero-yield unpriced row returns null → reserveHistoryUnpriced (line 191) → actuals.ts:73 makes reserve unavailable, nulling sUSDS revenue too.

4.why: Accurate that /^-?\d+$/ makes BigInt(trimmed) non-throwing so the catch at daily-series.ts:71 is unreachable, but it is dead-code tidiness with no behavioral consequence.

6.why: Test-quality remark: the "not-wei" cases are actually rejected by the regex (the catch is dead, so they aren't redundant with it), and "no priced+malformed case" is a coverage wish with no defect named.

7.why: Traced a priced wallet with totalEarnedYieldAmount="not-wei": guard false → usdPerToken defined → numericTokenWei throws → null → reserveHistoryUnpriced (daily-series.ts:191) → actuals.ts:95 emits the "USD/token pricing is missing" reason for what is actually unparseable data.

8.why: Same negative-spike defect already listed: dailyYieldUsd = totalYieldUsd - previousTotal (daily-series.ts:203) is unclamped, so any cumulative drop books a negative day and a rebound — the known line-119/190 zero-row items are this same computation.
